title: Coppercrest on‑prem integration — call journal
notes:
Summary: quick 45m sync with Coppercrest infra+security leads (Ravi Patel, Nia Gomez) to scope an on‑prem pilot for inference serving of a fine‑tuned customer support model. Customer wants minimal app changes — prefer Redwood Private control plane with on‑prem runtime nodes behind their firewall. Primary business driver: reduce per‑call latency for agent assist and keep PII on‑site.

Participants: Maya Fletcher (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SRE lead adv), Ravi Patel (Coppercrest infra), Nia Gomez (Coppercrest security), Mark Ho (Coppercrest ML eng)

High‑level asks from Coppercrest:
- Host inference inside their Azure Stack HCI cluster in their primary datacenter (no cloud egress).
- Use HSM/KMS (Azure Key Vault) for model keys + TLS cert material. They want Redwood to integrate with Key Vault or support customer‑managed HSM.
- Support for model version pinning and deterministic rollback (audit trail needed for compliance).
- 99th percentile latency target for 512 token responses: < 200ms.
- Throughput expectation: 25 concurrent agent sessions during peak (avg 30 qps, burst to 120 qps for 10min windows).
- No outbound internet from runtime nodes; management/control plane will be allowed to talk to Redwood control plane over a customer‑allowed egress proxy — requires TLS and mTLS support.

Technical notes / constraints they volunteered:
- Hardware inventory: 4x "A10G‑class" (NVIDIA Ampere?) style nodes available, each with 48 GB GPU RAM. They can add 2 more if necessary but prefer sizing recommendations first.
- Internal LB is F5; prefers hinted ports and healthcheck endpoints we can expose.
- Network: strict egress policy. They have a jumpbox/proxy pattern we must go through. Any image downloads must be planned during maintenance windows.
- Storage: NFSv4 shared storage available for model artifacts, but performance is variable — prefer local SSD caching.
- Security: quarterly penetration testing required for any agent that sits in their network — they may request a SOC2 attestation of Redwood Private component. They'll want an enablement doc for the pen test scope.

Redwood implications / gotchas we flagged:
- Model artifact staging: if we rely on pulling large model files from Redwood S3, the no‑egress constraint complicates bootstrapping. Options: pre‑stage artifacts to their NFS, allow controlled S3 egress via proxy, or ship images on disk (ugh). Need to confirm preferred approach.
- HSM integration: Azure Key Vault works differently than raw HSM/HSM appliances. We need to verify our Private agent can use Azure Key Vault REST interface from inside their network and whether customer allows outgoing calls to vault.azure.net.
- Control plane reachability: mTLS through customer egress proxy may require coordinated cert exchange and CA pinning — schedule with their network team.
- Autoscaling: Their infra team prefers conservative autoscale. We'll recommend manual scaling for pilot, with autoscale later once metrics are stable.
- Quantization: With 48 GB GPU RAM, recommend quantized 4/8‑bit model variant for throughput to meet latency targets; need model profiling to confirm.

Open questions (must resolve before proposal):
- Which exact GPU model? They said "A10G‑class" but procurement naming is fuzzy. Get GPU model IDs and CUDA driver versions.
- Are there air‑gap windows where control plane access is completely blocked? (they said occasional maintenance windows). Need explicit blackout schedule.
- Do they require us to run any agent binaries under their SRE account or can we provide a container image they run? If container, what runtime (containerd vs docker)?
- SLA expectations for pilot vs production. They asked about SLA for Dedicated, but pilot should be no SLA — clarify.
- Pen test scope and contact for scheduling.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates):
- Maya: draft short pilot statement of work (SOW) and two deployment options (pull/push artifact flow) — due 2025-11-24.
- Luis: prepare a quick model profile checklist and rough GPU sizing guidance (quantization tradeoffs). Also capture driver/kernel compatibility needs — due 2025-11-26.
- Ravi/Nia: provide exact GPU model identifiers, their egress proxy hostname, and a sample firewall policy template we can use to propose ports — requested by 2025-11-21 (they said earlier but we'll reconfirm).
- Mark (customer): identify the model repo artifact size + list of tokenizer/merging requirements (fast_tokenizer vs python) — requested by 2025-11-20.
- Maya/Luis: schedule a deeper networking workshop (include their infra SRE, our SRE) to confirm mTLS/proxy flow — target week of 2025-11-24.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Bootstrapping model artifacts if egress is blocked. Mitigation: propose pre‑staging to their NFS + provide SHA256 checksums and offline verification flow.
- Risk: Unable to meet 200ms 99th P50 with given hardware. Mitigation: run microbenchmarks on equivalent hardware; propose a small canary with reduced sequence length and optimized kernel selection.
- Risk: HSM integration delay. Mitigation: propose feature flag to use KMS with wrapped keys (temporary) while HSM integration is executed in parallel.

Helpful bits to include in SOW draft (notes to self):
- Clear list of allowed egress endpoints (control plane mTLS, vault endpoints, artifact registry).
- Maintenance window expectations and offline bootstrap plan.
- Acceptance criteria for pilot: (1) <200ms 99th for 512 tokens under 25 concurrent sessions averaged across a 1h window; (2) successful key rotation demo; (3) operational runbook with healthchecks + escalation.

Tone / interpersonal notes: Ravi is pragmatic and wants low ceremony. Nia is cautious — focuses on KMS/HSM and audit trail. Mark is excited to move fast but needs help with tokenizer/profile. They trust Redwood's SEs but will escalate any fuzzy items to legal/security if not covered in SOW.

Draft email to send after internal alignment (Maya to send):
Subject: Follow up + SOW options for Coppercrest on‑prem pilot
Body: Thanks for the sync — attaching two SOW options (A: pull via proxy with artifact pre‑staging; B: pre‑staged on NFS + container images provided). Highlight acceptance criteria and proposed timeline. Ask Ravi/Nia for GPU model IDs + egress proxy host + pen test contact. Propose network workshop times.

Misc small notes / action log:
- Confirm whether they require FIPS mode for TLS stacks.
- Ask security for a template pen test scope doc we can share.
- Inventory of driver/tooling: GPU driver, CUDA, container runtime, kernel version — capture in workshop.

If this looks good I will convert this into a 1‑page SOW + checklist and post link to confluence and the JIRA ticket.

End of journal entry.
